```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(coherentSurv)
```

This runnable example translates a synthetic event-history model into credit
terminology. It uses no borrower data and provides no external validation for
lending, pricing, capital or intervention decisions. The parameters below are
illustrative; renaming simulated events does not establish a realistic credit
model.

## Define the analysis before mapping the records

An independent unit is one synthetic account. Recurrent marks represent
separate delinquency episodes and covenant breaches, with follow-up in years.
The terminal event is the first default under the analyst's definition, after
which this analysis stops counting events. An account that can cure and return
to the risk set would need a different state/eligibility specification; a
recoverable delinquency status is not automatically an absorbing default.

The simulator below uses the existing `cs_simulate()` engine. Its baseline
covariate is a Bernoulli group indicator, labelled `leverage_group` for this
example, rather than an estimated debt ratio. At each jump, each intensity is
the shared gamma frailty times its baseline rate times
`exp(beta * leverage_group + history * sum(capped prior counts))`.
The cap is one prior event per recurrent mark. Actual future counts remain
uncapped. Independent censoring has rate 0.04 per year and administrative
follow-up ends after four years. All retained event times are exact in this
synthetic experiment; quarterly reporting windows are not fabricated from
them.

```{r credit-generator}
sim_credit_portfolio <- function(n = 120L, max_years = 4, seed = 808L) {
  d <- cs_simulate(
    n = n, horizon = max_years,
    rates = c(0.50, 0.30, 0.18),
    beta = c(0.25, 0.15, 0.35),
    history = c(0.12, 0.10, 0.20),
    dispersion = 0.40, censor_rate = 0.04,
    history_cap = 1L, seed = seed, time_unit = "years"
  )
  d$account_id <- sprintf("ACCT-%04d", d$id)
  d$id <- NULL
  names(d)[names(d) == "x"] <- "leverage_group"
  labels <- c("0", "delinquency", "covenant_breach")
  d$event_type <- labels[d$event_type + 1L]
  d
}

credit <- sim_credit_portfolio()
head(credit, 6)
attr(credit, "truth")
```

## Fit on complete training-account histories

The split below is fixed by account identifier before inspecting outcomes.
All intervals from an account stay in the same split. To keep the example
compact, the frailty variance is fixed at its generating value, 0.40; this is
a disclosed simulation choice, not a way to learn an unknown real portfolio's
heterogeneity. The remaining coefficients are estimated. Optimizer and
regularity diagnostics remain visible.

```{r credit-fit}
account_ids <- unique(credit$account_id)
training_ids <- account_ids[seq_len(90L)]
evaluation_ids <- account_ids[-seq_len(90L)]
training <- credit[credit$account_id %in% training_ids, , drop = FALSE]

training_trajectory <- cs_as_trajectory(
  training, unit = "account_id", start = "start", stop = "stop",
  event_type = "event_type", terminal = "terminal", observed = "observed",
  event_types = c("delinquency", "covenant_breach"), time_unit = "years"
)
fit_credit <- cs_fit(
  ~ leverage_group, data = training_trajectory, unit = "account_id",
  observed = "observed", event_types = c("delinquency", "covenant_breach"),
  time_unit = "years", frailty = "gamma",
  control = cs_control(phi_fixed = 0.40, history_cap = 1L, maxit = 200L)
)
fit_credit$convergence
```

This fit assumes the declared exact observation process and working intensity
model. Real bureau reporting can involve uncertain times, incomplete counts,
changing exposure and informative account closure. Those features require
their own observation and statistical treatment; merely relabelling interval
endpoints as report dates does not supply it.

## Forecast using only eligible histories through one year

An evaluation account must still be observed and default-free at the landmark.
We retain only its history through that time. A follow-up interval crossing
the landmark is truncated and its later endpoint event is removed. Eligibility
uses no event after the landmark; the future outcomes of the held-out accounts
are not inputs to these forecasts. The baseline group is frozen, as explicitly
requested in `predict()`.

```{r credit-landmark}
landmark <- 1
evaluation <- credit[credit$account_id %in% evaluation_ids, , drop = FALSE]
by_account <- split(evaluation, evaluation$account_id)
eligible <- vapply(by_account, function(g) {
  max(g$stop) >= landmark &&
    !any(g$terminal == 1L & g$stop <= landmark)
}, logical(1))
eligible_ids <- names(eligible)[eligible]
stopifnot(length(eligible_ids) >= 3L)

history_at_landmark <- evaluation[
  evaluation$account_id %in% eligible_ids & evaluation$start < landmark,
  , drop = FALSE
]
crosses_landmark <- history_at_landmark$stop > landmark
history_at_landmark$stop[crosses_landmark] <- landmark
history_at_landmark$event_type[crosses_landmark] <- "0"
history_at_landmark$terminal[crosses_landmark] <- 0L
stopifnot(
  all(history_at_landmark$stop <= landmark),
  all(history_at_landmark$terminal == 0L),
  all(tapply(history_at_landmark$stop,
             history_at_landmark$account_id, max) == landmark)
)

# Display three accounts selected by identifier, not forecast or later outcome.
forecast_history <- history_at_landmark[
  history_at_landmark$account_id %in% head(eligible_ids, 3L), , drop = FALSE
]
forecast <- predict(
  fit_credit, newdata = forecast_history, landmark = landmark,
  horizon = c(0.5, 1, 2), type = "all", covariate_evolution = "freeze"
)
forecast[forecast$unit == forecast$unit[1L],
         c("unit", "landmark", "horizon", "target", "estimate", "time_unit")]
```

`risk` is default probability over the future horizon; `survival` is its
complement. The two `burden_*` outputs are expected additional episode counts,
not episode probabilities or monetary severity. `rmst` is expected time before
default restricted to the horizon:

\[
 E\{\min(T_D-s,\Delta)\mid T_D>s,\mathcal H_s\}
 =\int_0^\Delta P(T_D>s+u\mid T_D>s,\mathcal H_s)\,du.
\]

This is restricted **pre-default account life**, sometimes called performing
life. In this example it includes time spent delinquent before default; it is
not time with all payments current. It is also not the unrestricted mean time
to default. All these predictions arise from the same fitted law, with counts
stopping at default. We can check their basic identities directly.

```{r credit-coherence}
keys <- c("unit", "landmark", "horizon")
risk <- forecast[forecast$target == "risk", c(keys, "estimate")]
survival <- forecast[forecast$target == "survival", c(keys, "estimate")]
paired <- merge(risk, survival, by = keys, suffixes = c("_risk", "_survival"))
restricted_life <- forecast[forecast$target == "rmst", ]
stopifnot(
  max(abs(paired$estimate_risk + paired$estimate_survival - 1)) < 1e-8,
  all(forecast$estimate >= -1e-10),
  all(restricted_life$estimate <= restricted_life$horizon + 1e-8)
)
```

The returned series, roundoff and frailty-compression diagnostics concern
numerical approximation. These likelihood-based point forecasts do not supply
individual-history confidence intervals through a `std_error` field. A small
synthetic held-out sample does not establish calibration in a real credit
population.

## Supply exposure and loss severity separately

Default probability alone is not expected monetary loss. For a deliberately
simple undiscounted scenario with fixed exposure at default (EAD) and fixed
loss given default (LGD), conditional expected default loss is
`PD * EAD * LGD`. Here EAD and LGD are supplied assumptions, not fitted outputs.

```{r credit-loss}
one_year <- risk[risk$horizon == 1, c("unit", "estimate")]
names(one_year)[2L] <- "default_probability"
one_year$exposure_at_default <- 100000
one_year$loss_given_default <- 0.40
one_year$expected_default_loss <- with(
  one_year, default_probability * exposure_at_default * loss_given_default
)
one_year
```

Amounts above are illustrative monetary units. With changing or uncertain EAD,
LGD, recovery times or discounting, the required target is the expectation of
the joint loss reward, not generally a product of separate marginal means.
Recurrent delinquency counts do not estimate claim severity or LGD. Any
additional per-episode costs must exclude components already included in the
default-loss reward to avoid double counting. Parameter, price and severity
uncertainty are not included in this table, and it estimates no causal savings
from an intervention.

## A separate finite-support recording-sensitivity example

The next calculation is a distinct toy population, not a correction applied to
`fit_credit` or to the account forecasts. Its complete histories are assumed to
belong to exactly four declared atoms. The reward is a default indicator, with
no model-estimated probabilities supplied as category rewards. The counts are
an illustrative recorded sample, not extracted from the simulated portfolio.

```{r credit-recording-law}
support <- data.frame(
  complete_history = c("no episodes; no default", "delinquency; no default",
                       "covenant breach; default", "two distress episodes; default"),
  default = c(0, 0, 1, 1),
  recorded_count = c(50L, 30L, 15L, 5L)
)
p_recorded <- support$recorded_count / sum(support$recorded_count)
support

bounded <- cs_bounds(
  p = p_recorded, numerator = support$default,
  kappa = 1.75, recording_fraction = 0.80,
  counts = support$recorded_count, alpha = 0.05
)
stopifnot(is.list(bounded$outer))
data.frame(
  layer = c("Identification bounds at recorded empirical law",
            "Outer projection including recorded-count uncertainty"),
  lower = c(bounded$lower, bounded$outer$lower),
  upper = c(bounded$upper, bounded$outer$upper)
)

# The structural solver targets the same declared finite problem.
sparse_bounded <- cs_bounds_sparse(
  p = p_recorded, numerator = support$default,
  kappa = 1.75, recording_fraction = 0.80,
  counts = support$recorded_count, alpha = 0.05
)
stopifnot(max(abs(c(bounded$lower, bounded$upper) -
                    c(sparse_bounded$lower, sparse_bounded$upper))) < 1e-8)
bounded$assumptions
```

Here 0.80 is a specified probability of recording a **complete history**, not
the percentage of individual delinquency events captured. `p_recorded` is the
category distribution conditional on recording. `kappa` restricts marginal
recording odds under this finite model; it is neither a fitted macroeconomic
stress coefficient nor a causal policy effect. For independent recorded
histories with these category counts and the stated recording assumptions, `outer` projects a
simultaneous recorded-law confidence region, separately from the identification
bounds. The support, recording fraction and sensitivity restriction remain
assumed. Neither solver discovers missing credit events, unknown history types
or the recording fraction from the fitted portfolio.
